issues.what: The orange demo ends on Eya's takeaway that the phases changed because SHE moved, and nobody corrects it. In the sky it is the moon that orbits the Earth
issues.quote: Only what I could see changed! Because I moved!

issues.what: On the last night of Ramadan the full moon was about two weeks ago, not last week
issues.quote: Last week it was big and round.

issues.what: Eya wears pink trainers; the slippers are Mongi's
issues.quote: Eya stepped sideways. Slippers scuffing.

issues.what: 'Another' baby cried, but there was no first baby
issues.quote: Another baby cried.

fix: Chapter 1: Mongi's reply should say the moon circles the Earth once a month and the sun always lights one half. Change 'last week' to 'two weeks ago', 'slippers' to 'trainers', and 'Another baby' to 'A baby'.
praise: The orange-and-lamp scene makes phases concrete for a 7-year-old, and the crescent's bright side facing the sunset is exactly right.

issues.what: No dialogue in any chapter has quotation marks, so a young reader cannot tell speech from narration
issues.quote: Just buy new tiles, he said. Easy.

issues.what: Wrong maths: six equilateral triangles round a point make a hexagon, not a star (also ch2)
issues.quote: Two made a diamond. Six made a star.

issues.what: The 'five-sided shapes never fit' lesson is only true for regular pentagons, and a house-shaped pentagon does tile; the story never says the sides are equal
issues.quote: A pentagon. Like a little house without a roof.

issues.what: The stars that fill pentagon gaps have eight points; pentagon patterns use five-pointed stars (a 36-degree gap is one star point)
issues.quote: Eight thin points.

issues.what: The mirror, spinning star, floor tiling and pentagon gaps are each replayed in ch3, 4 and 5 as if they were new ('Oh! Now I see the whole flower', 'Add little stars!')
issues.quote: Hey! said Zulfiya. No matter how we push, holes stay.

issues.what: Ch3 and ch4 end on the same question about the centre star's colour
issues.quote: what color should we paint the very center star

issues.what: Timeline: ch5 opens 'Today was Navruz', then glazes and fires the tile, then later 'On Navruz morning'. Ch1 says Navruz is ten days away, but the story covers five days
issues.quote: Today was Navruz. Today the gate would be whole.

issues.what: A glass mirror glued into the tile before firing would melt in the kiln, and the children stand close enough that the kiln heat hugs their faces
issues.quote: Zulfiya glued the tiny mirror in the center with care.

issues.what: Three flowers are broken but only one is remade. Brief text leaks in the present tense ('He is ten', 'she always asks'). Ch2 title 'The Folded Paper' belongs to ch1
issues.quote: Three blue flowers were broken in half.

fix: Add quotation marks to every line of dialogue in ch1-5. Ch1-2: six triangles make a hexagon; state that the sides are equal; give the stars five points and a corner reason. Ch3-5: cut or reframe the repeated demos (ch4 checks the drawing against a measured string). Ch5 happens the day before Navruz, the kiln fires overnight, the mirror goes in after firing and the children stand back. Remove ch3's duplicate last line. One broken flower, Navruz in five days. Retitle ch2, ch4 and ch5.
praise: Bahodir's mirror down the middle of a broken flower is a lovely, true way to teach symmetry, and Sanjar's turn from rival to helper is sweet.

issues.what: Chapter 3 is titled 'The Candlelit Dinner', but the dinner is in ch2; ch3 is hatching night
issues.quote: September came at last.

issues.what: Hawksbills crawl with an alternating gait, so their flipper marks are staggered, not two matching parallel lines
issues.quote: two long lines. They looked like tiny tractor wheels, one on each side

issues.what: Ch3 opens with a recap of ch1 and ch2 (tracks, thermometer, calendar) told as dialogue
issues.quote: You remember the first morning?

fix: Retitle ch3 'Hatching Night'. Describe the tracks as alternating flipper marks in ch1 and in the ch3 callback.
praise: The turtle science is accurate throughout (temperature and sex, about two months, brightest horizon, red light, hands off), and Lorna is persuaded, not shamed.

issues.what: Both chapters are titled 'Six Pennies'
issues.quote: Six Pennies

issues.what: A child cannot feel squeeze and stretch by running a finger along a slightly bent craft stick. The fact is true but the demonstration is not
issues.quote: The top feels squished together. The bottom feels pulled long.

issues.what: Josefina's line claims triangles help her arch and blocks help his triangles, which is not true
issues.quote: Your triangles help my arch. My blocks help your triangles.

issues.what: The brief says Grandma calls every bridge by its first name, but she never names the yellow bridge
issues.quote: Say hi to this old friend.

fix: Retitle ch2. Replace the stick-bend with a foam strip marked with lines (top bunches, bottom spreads) and echo it in ch2. Fix Josefina's team line. Grandma names the bridge.
praise: Triangles lock and squares tilt, and arches push out and need strong ends: both are shown with sticks and pennies, and the 'I quit' running joke pays off.

issues.what: The key idea is backwards: a satellite low on the horizon at the start of a pass is at its farthest and faintest, and loudest when overhead. The aunt's 'middle of the pass, close' was correct and Faraji's 'low and loud' is wrong, then repeated in ch3 and ch4
issues.quote: At the start of the pass, when he is lowest and loudest!

issues.what: A milk-carton-sized satellite is far too faint to see with the naked eye, but the children watch it as a 'moving star' in ch1, ch3 and ch4
issues.quote: That is him. He goes all the way round the Earth

issues.what: Pass count breaks: Mwanaisha pockets a stone for a pass that never happened ('No beep tonight'), so the four passes do not add up
issues.quote: She took one stone and put it in her pocket.

issues.what: 6-year-old Faraji climbs the rooftop water tank in ch1, ch2 and ch4. Readers could copy this
issues.quote: Faraji climbed up the water tank. He could climb anything.

issues.what: Ch3 re-teaches the ninety-minute orbit as if it were new ('Her mouth fell open')
issues.quote: He goes all the way round the Earth? she whispered.

issues.what: Ch2 title 'The Rusty Dish' nearly duplicates ch1 'The Rusty TV Dish'
issues.quote: The Rusty Dish

issues.what: Malindi is their town, so the photo line makes no sense
issues.quote: That bend is Malindi! That tiny dot is our town!

fix: Ch2-4: make Faraji's idea 'closest = loudest', so they send in the middle of the pass when Kijana is overhead. Ch1: the moving star is the space station and Kijana is too small to see; ch3-4 find him by ear. Three passes, two stones after ch1, no stone used in ch2. No climbing the tank. Retitle ch2 and ch3.
praise: Warm and funny, with a real engineering puzzle: the up-and-down power graph that shows the spin is a lovely deduction for a 9-year-old.

issues.what: Timeline is a day out: Hira catches him on the 'third night', and the next evening Mahnoor says the rehearsal is tomorrow and the mehndi the day after, which puts the mehndi on day five of four
issues.quote: On the third night Hira caught him.

issues.what: A Naat (a devotional poem praising the Prophet) is played as a joke that turns into bhangra. This is disrespectful
issues.quote: a Naat gone wrong turned into bhangra

issues.what: Brand names
issues.quote: between the parked Corolla ... a bottle of Pakola

issues.what: His sandals were polished for the mehndi, so they cannot be 'dusty with roof dust'
issues.quote: His sandals were dusty with roof dust and now grass.

issues.what: Title 'Tomorrow's Rehearsal' undersells a chapter with the knee injury and the mehndi
issues.quote: Tomorrow's Rehearsal

fix: Ch1: 'second night' and replace the Naat joke. Ch2: remove brands, fix the sandals, retitle.
praise: A dry, loving narrator. 'That was his happy' and the 'always in a meeting' line coming back from Hira land perfectly.

issues.what: Orbital speed at 410 km is about 7.7 km/s, not 11
issues.quote: eleven kilometres every second

issues.what: 'Two zero metres' is the 20 m HF band, which a solar storm would black out. Astronauts talk to hams on two metres
issues.quote: on two zero metres calling blind

issues.what: The pass times contradict Jory's correction: he moves the passes four minutes later, but they still arrive at Wenna's uncorrected times, and the last one comes four minutes earlier (06:12 against 06:16)
issues.quote: At 06:12 the hiss rose.

issues.what: Plasma is seen straight after the burn ends. Entry comes about half an hour after a deorbit burn
issues.quote: We see plasma. Orange outside. Gotta go.

issues.what: Brand name (Yaesu). 'Leisure battery' becomes 'car battery' later in the chapter. The title 'First Pass' covers the whole night. A Newlyn trawler has a Bristol accent
issues.quote: It was an old Yaesu she ran off a leisure battery

issues.what: A burn over Cornwall would bring the capsule down thousands of kilometres downrange, not near a Newlyn trawler. This is set by the brief, so it is left and flagged
issues.quote: three parachutes, big orange ones, coming down east of us

fix: Chapter 1: fix the speed, the band and the period; set the passes at 03:10/04:42/06:14 before Jory's fix and 03:14/04:46/06:18 after; move the plasma to later; remove the brand; car battery; retitle.
praise: The grandmother and grandson checking each other's sums by candlelight, and 'would not need to stop', give a disaster story a warm, human centre.
